method: Review the lesson text, metadata checkpoints, registered provider and circuit-breaker sources, and execute all Python fences. Run the offline assertion script. No provider requests or archived provider runs were made.

observations.trace: Corrected the fixed-input and growing-context arithmetic; separated request output limits, task budgets, account/project caps and dependency breakers; added request-time reservation and response-time reconciliation; constrained partial results by task contract; scoped historical usage fields to their provider snapshot; revised the breaker demo labels to match actual execution; and removed unsupported universal P99 and weekly-doubling thresholds.

limitations: No live provider request, model behavior, billing reconciliation, or production budget enforcement was tested.
The historical DeepSeek usage snapshot remains a local normalized replay; archived raw requests and responses were not reproduced.

The first Python example is a toy simulation that counts fixed successful-call resource amounts and excludes failed-call cost, account quotas, distributed breaker state, timeouts, and half-open probing.
The offline assertions verify editorial boundaries and displayed code behavior, not that the proposed policy is appropriate for every task or workload.
